stem: Over the same five days, the daily high temperatures, in degrees Celsius, were 20, 21, 22, 23 and 24 in Town P and 12, 22, 22, 22 and 32 in Town Q. Which statement about the standard deviations of the two data sets is true?

choices.A: The standard deviations are equal, because the two data sets have the same mean.
choices.B: Town Q's temperatures have the greater standard deviation.
choices.C: The standard deviations are equal, because the two data sets have the same median.
choices.D: Town P's temperatures have the greater standard deviation.

solution: Both data sets have a mean of 22, so compare how far the values are from 22.
In Town P every value is within 2 degrees of 22. In Town Q two values are 10 degrees away from 22.
The values for Town Q are more spread out from the mean, so Town Q has the greater standard deviation.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The means are equal (22), but data sets with the same mean can be spread out differently. Town Q's values are farther from 22.
explanation.B: Correct. Both means are 22, and Town Q has two values 10 degrees from the mean, while every Town P value is within 2 degrees of it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The medians are equal (22), but the median says nothing about spread. Town Q's values are farther from the center.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Town P has more different values, but they are all close to the mean of 22. Standard deviation measures distance from the mean, not how many different values there are.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'C': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'D': 'C', 'A': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'C', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'D', 'D': 'A'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
sd = lambda d: sqrt(sum((x - Rational(sum(d), len(d)))**2 for x in d) / len(d))
ssd = lambda d: sqrt(sum((x - Rational(sum(d), len(d)))**2 for x in d) / (len(d) - 1))
P = [20, 21, 22, 23, 24]
Q = [12, 22, 22, 22, 32]
assert sum(P) == sum(Q) and sorted(P)[2] == sorted(Q)[2]
assert sd(Q) > sd(P) and ssd(Q) > ssd(P)
assert choices[answer].startswith("Town Q")
